De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) is the central bank, supervisor and resolution authority that works for financial stability and sustainable prosperity in the Netherlands. In this way, DNB, together with European partners, contributes to price stability and balanced macroeconomic development in Europe, a shock-resistant financial system, secure and reliable payments, and sound financial institutions that meet their obligations and commitments. To strengthen the policy aimed at these objectives, DNB regularly issues independent economic advice. DNB is also responsible for payments in Caribisch Nederland. DNB also works with the Depositogarantiefonds to implement the deposit guarantee scheme in Caribisch Nederland. Together with the Autoriteit Financiële Markten (AFM), DNB supervises financial institutions located in Caribisch Nederland.

Statutory task: As an independent administrative body (zbo), De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) has the following tasks under article 4 of the Bankwet 1998:* supervising financial institutions under the applicable statutory rules;* promoting the smooth operation of payments;* promoting the stability of the financial system;* collecting statistical data and producing statistics under the applicable statutory rules;* carrying out resolution tasks relating to certain financial undertakings in accordance with the applicable statutory rules. DNB can, after permission by Koninklijk Besluit, also carry out tasks in the general interest other than those named in the Bankwet 1998. In addition to its zbo tasks set out in article 4 of the Bankwet 1998, DNB has the monetary tasks included in article 3 of the Bankwet 1998. Thus DNB is the central bank of the Netherlands and in that capacity (as a participant in the European System of Central Banks) is charged with tasks to implement the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. As central bank, DNB is fully independent of the minister of Financiën. Finally, DNB is responsible for payments in Caribisch Nederland. DNB works with both the Depositogarantiefonds and the Autoriteit Financiële Markten (AFM), respectively to implement the deposit guarantee scheme in Caribisch Nederland and to supervise financial institutions in Caribisch Nederland.

Statutory task: * Handling air traffic safely and efficiently at and around the airports Amsterdam Airport Schiphol, Rotterdam Airport, Groningen Airport Eelde and Maastricht Aachen Airport and above the Netherlands up to 24,500 feet;* renewing and managing technical systems; * providing aeronautical information; * providing training for air traffic control; * providing aeronautical charts and publications.

The Mondriaan Fonds arose from the merger on 30 December 2011 of the Fonds BKVB, which focused on contemporary artists and intermediaries, and the Mondriaan Stichting, which focused on institutions in the field of visual art and cultural heritage.

Statutory task: The Mondriaan Fonds is the public fund for the promotion of visual art and cultural heritage. It promotes exceptional and innovative projects and activities of visual artists, intermediaries and institutions that are important for visual art and cultural heritage in the Netherlands. All financial contributions the Mondriaan Fonds provides aim to stimulate the meaningful development and visibility of visual art and cultural heritage in the Netherlands where the market does not, or does not yet, make this possible.

The Nationaal Rapporteur Mensenhandel en Seksueel Geweld tegen Kinderen is independent and has the statutory task of researching the nature and extent of human trafficking and sexual violence against children. It also has the statutory task of researching the effects of current policy on tackling human trafficking and sexual violence against children, and of advising the government on preventing and combating them.The Netherlands has had a Nationaal Rapporteur working on human trafficking since 2000. In 2009 the mandate was extended to tackling child pornography. In the first report on this mandate in 2011, the Nationaal Rapporteur concluded that tackling child pornography should be seen more broadly, in the context of sexual violence against children. The Dutch government then adopted this recommendation, which led in 2012 to the mandate being extended to sexual violence against children.The Nationaal Rapporteur is supported in their work by a bureau. Together with the bureau, the Nationaal Rapporteur forms the institute Nationaal Rapporteur Mensenhandel en Seksueel Geweld tegen Kinderen; the institute functions as a zelfstandig bestuursorgaan.

Statutory task: * researching the nature and extent of human trafficking and sexual violence against children;* researching the effects of policy intended to counter human trafficking and sexual violence against children;* advising national and local government and organisations in care services and criminal law on combating human trafficking and sexual violence against children;* sharing insights into the issue with members of the Tweede Kamer and municipalities.

Before 2017 this zbo was called Stichting Nationale en Internationale Wegvervoer Organisatie. Because of the change from private law (Stichting) to public law, it is now Nationale en Internationale Wegvervoer Organisatie (NIWO).

Statutory task: Promoting Dutch domestic and cross-border professional road haulage by: * (pursuant to article 32 wgw) granting and withdrawing licences for domestic professional transport as referred to in article 8 and article 12, first paragraph, respectively;* granting and withdrawing Community licences as referred to in article 10, second and fourth paragraph, respectively;* granting and withdrawing authorisations to carry out cross-border transport as referred to in article 25, first paragraph;* issuing additional documents for cross-border professional transport as referred to in article 26, first paragraph and second paragraph, part c, respectively;* other work to be assigned by or under an algemene maatregel van bestuur, relating to both domestic and cross-border professional transport;* (pursuant to article 7 Besluit goederenvervoer over de weg) keeping a registration and alert system to implement the provisions of article 12 of the law;* managing data files for its public tasks;* taking part in negotiations under bilateral treaties with other states, or to conclude bilateral treaties;* the NIWO can be given other tasks by ministerial regulation, which in any case include the implementation of Regulation (EEC) number 391/90.

The Nederlands Instituut Publieke Veiligheid (NIPV) is a knowledge institute that focuses on, among other things, crisis management and fire services. Through research, education, information provision and support, the NIPV strengthens various crisis partners, including the veiligheidsregio's and central government.

Statutory task: The Nederlands Instituut Publieke Veiligheid (NIPV) has the following tasks:* providing officer training, as well as providing other training courses (to be designated by the minister of Justitie en Veiligheid) that end with an exam as referred to in article 18, paragraph 4 of the Wet veiligheidsregio's;* developing teaching, exercise and learning material for the above training courses;* developing and maintaining expertise, by collecting and managing relevant knowledge and, where necessary, by carrying out applied scientific research;* making the collected information and expertise available to organisations working in fire services, disaster control, crisis management and medical assistance;* acquiring and managing equipment (including gear and telecommunication facilities) and, where necessary, making it available to the veiligheidsregio's and municipalities with a municipal fire service;* carrying out other work in fire services, disaster control, crisis management and medical assistance, as regards providing training other than that referred to above and developing teaching, exercise and learning material for such training;* recruiting and selecting candidates for the above training courses;* organising exercises;* carrying out other activities that promote the expertise of persons within fire services, disaster control, crisis management and medical assistance (or the functioning of the organisations they work for);* carrying out research for, and advising, third parties in order to contribute directly or indirectly to physical safety.

Nederlands Meetinstituut N.V. (NMi) is designated in the Regeling meetmiddelen politie to examine police measuring instruments, such as speed meters, and to issue a certificate when they pass. A certificate normally lasts two years, one year for radar.

The Nederlands-Vlaamse Accreditatieorganisatie (NVAO) is responsible for accrediting existing and new programmes in higher education in Nederland and Vlaanderen. The NVAO also assesses the quality assurance of higher education institutions in Nederland and Vlaanderen, so that their quality is safeguarded in an expert and independent way.

Statutory task: The main tasks of the Nederlands-Vlaamse Accreditatieorganisatie (NVAO) are: * assessing and safeguarding the level and quality of higher education in Nederland and Vlaanderen; * promoting a culture of quality within higher education. The NVAO carries out these tasks from an international perspective and in the context of the European Bologna Process.

Statutory task: The registered pilots together form the Nederlandse loodsencorporatie (NLC). Membership of the corporation is compulsory and arises by operation of law. The NLC is a public professional body within the meaning of article 134 of the Grondwet. The corporation has regulatory powers over its members in a number of areas, such as training, professional practice and service provision. The regulations are enforced through disciplinary law, by the tuchtcollege loodsen. The corporation has three bodies: the chair, who represents the corporation externally, the general council, which forms the executive board, and the members' meeting, which adopts the regulations.

The Kaderwet zbo's does not apply because the body exercises no public authority (Tweede Kamer 2007-2008, 25268, number 50, statement by the minister of Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap).

Statutory task: TNO is an independent research organisation that, on the basis of its expertise and research, makes an important contribution to the competitiveness of companies and organisations, to the economy and to the quality of society as a whole.

The Nederlandse Organisatie voor Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek (NWO) ensures quality and innovation in science and is one of the most important funders of science in Nederland. Each year NWO invests almost 1 billion euros in curiosity-driven research, research aimed at societal challenges and research infrastructure. NWO selects and funds research proposals on the basis of advice from expert scientists and specialists from Nederland and abroad. NWO also has nine research institutes of its own, where internationally leading research is carried out. NWO stimulates national and international cooperation, invests in large research facilities and promotes the use of knowledge. NWO funds just over 7.000 research projects at universities and other knowledge institutions. NWO is an independent administrative body (zelfstandig bestuursorgaan) with tasks laid down by law. The organisation falls under the responsibility of the ministerie van Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap. The executive board bears final responsibility for carrying out the tasks of the whole umbrella organisation. The supervisory board advises the executive board (RvB) on request or on its own initiative and has an audit committee that advises the executive board on the budget, the annual accounts and the annual report. The advisory council can advise the executive board, on request or on its own initiative, on developments in society and science that are relevant to NWO. Domain boards, research institutes and coordinating bodies (temporary steering bodies) fall under the executive board. The quality, care and transparency of the assessment process and project management are important to NWO. The governance of NWO is laid down in the NWO-wet and regulations. For reasons of good governance, quality, care and transparency, the NWO subsidy regulation and a number of internal regulations have been adopted. The NWO domains, research institutes and coordinating bodies carry out NWO's core task: promoting quality and innovation in science. The NWO domains organise the programmes and funding for research. Both the executive board and the NWO domain boards have the power to distribute public funds for scientific research. Research is carried out at the NWO institutes. Coordinating bodies are temporary units with special attention for one, often multidisciplinary, field of research.

Statutory task: NWO's task is to promote the quality of scientific research and to initiate and stimulate new developments in scientific research. NWO carries out its task in particular by allocating resources. The organisation promotes the transfer of knowledge of the results of research it has initiated and stimulated, for the benefit of society. In carrying out its task, NWO focuses mainly on university research. In doing so it pays attention to coordination and promotes it where necessary.

The Nederlandse Publieke Omroep (NPO) is the steering and cooperation body responsible for carrying out the public media tasks at national level, as laid down in the Mediawet 2008.

Statutory task: The main tasks of the Nederlandse Publieke Omroep (NPO) are:* promoting cooperation and coordination within the national public broadcasting system;* allocating the airtime of institutions that have obtained national public airtime;* funding the institutions that have obtained national public airtime.

The Nederlandse Transplantatie Stichting (NTS) works to improve organ and tissue donation and transplantation. It supports the donor hospitals and transplant centres in Nederland. Since the introduction of the Wet op de orgaandonatie in 1997, the NTS has had the task of guiding donation and transplantation properly. It does this on behalf of the ministerie van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport (VWS).

Statutory task: The Nederlandse Transplantatie Stichting (NTS) has the following tasks and powers under the Wet op de orgaandonatie:* mediating in obtaining donor organs;* mediating in typing donor organs;* mediating in transporting donor organs;* allocating donor organs to a suitable recipient.

Statutory task: The Nederlandse Zorgautoriteit (NZa) is charged with:* market supervision, market development and tariff and performance regulation in the field of health care;* supervising the lawful implementation by health insurers of what is regulated by or under the Zorgverzekeringswet; * supervising the lawful settlement of the contributions referred to in articles 32 to 34 of the Zorgverzekeringswet, after an insurer has stopped providing health insurance; * supervising the lawful and effective implementation by the AWBZ insurers and the legal entities referred to in article 40 of the Algemene Wet Bijzondere Ziektekosten of what is regulated by or under that act and articles 91, second paragraph, second sentence, 123 and 124 of the Wet financiering sociale verzekeringen; * supervising the implementation of articles 41, 42 and 43 of the Wet marktordening gezondheidszorg. Article 3 of this act lays down the legal basis of the NZa. The NZa focuses, besides the funding of care providers and monitoring the proper implementation of insurance laws in health care, on proactively setting conditions for market forces and enforcing them. The aim of the new health care system is that consumers get value for their money. Efficiency, choice, quality and accessibility of care markets are central to this.

Nuffic helps schools and educational institutions in Nederland and abroad to make international education and cooperation possible. In addition, Nuffic is responsible in Nederland for the work of the Nationaal Agentschap Erasmus+ Onderwijs & Training.

Statutory task: Nuffic is the organisation in Nederland that deals with the internationalisation of education. As a zbo, Nuffic is responsible for carrying out the tasks of the Nationaal Agentschap Erasmus+ Onderwijs & Training.

The Onderzoeksraad voor Veiligheid (OVV) investigates accidents and disasters in Nederland, with the aim of preventing them from happening again. As of 1 February 2005 the OVV is the continuation of the former Raad voor de Transportveiligheid.

Statutory task: The Onderzoeksraad voor Veiligheid (OVV) has the task, with the sole aim of preventing future incidents or limiting their consequences, of investigating and establishing the causes or probable causes of individual incidents or categories of incidents and the extent of their consequences, and where necessary of making recommendations to improve safety. The OVV is authorised to investigate events in fields such as traffic and transport, defence, health, the environment, industry, construction and nature. For example, the OVV can investigate fires, explosions or natural disasters, but in principle all incidents are eligible for investigation. The only exceptions are incidents in the field of public order, counter-terrorism, peace missions, acts of war and the like. The OVV has jurisdiction for the whole Koninkrijk, so for Nederland, Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten.

ONVZ Langdurige Zorg B.V. is an implementing body of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), as referred to in article 4.1.1 of that act.

Statutory task: ONVZ Langdurige Zorg B.V. is responsible for carrying out the tasks described in section 2 of chapter 4 (articles 4.2.1 to 4.2.6) of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz).

Statutory task: * Issuing decisions on an application for recognition, an extraordinary pension, a guarantee supplement, a (periodic) benefit, a guarantee benefit, compensation, an allowance or a review as referred to in the laws for resistance participants and war victims, made by a person who does not yet derive or has not derived a financial entitlement from the law on which the application is based; * Reviewing, on its own initiative, recognition as a resistance participant, persecuted person or civilian victim; * Setting policy rules for decisions of the Sociale Verzekeringsbank as referred to in article 6 (parts a, b and d); * Advising the Sociale Verzekeringsbank on decisions that cannot be taken on the basis of the policy rules referred to in part c.

Statutory task: * Supporting national recruitment and carrying out selection;* providing initial and post-initial police education (including examinations);* transferring knowledge to the Nederlandse politie and contributing to the development of the performance of the police task, among other things by carrying out research;* developing and providing training other than initial or post-initial education;* In addition, the Politieacademie may carry out market activities (see article 3 paragraph 2 of the Wet op het LSOP), provided that this work is related to the tasks above, does not lead to distortion of competition with private providers of comparable services and is carried out at prices that at least cover costs.

Accreditation is the assessment of whether a testing body, certification body, inspection body or laboratory (conformity assessment bodies) carries out its work impartially and competently. After a positive assessment, the accreditation body issues a formal statement that the body meets the requirements set by European harmonised standards (Staatscourant 2010, 3033) and, where applicable, by additional requirements.

Statutory task: * Carrying out the tasks assigned in regulation (EC) number 765/2008 (on accreditation and market surveillance). This includes assessing the competence of conformity assessment bodies to carry out a specific conformity assessment activity, * monitoring the conformity assessment bodies that have been granted an accreditation certificate * and the work in the context of peer evaluation.

As of 1 February 2006 the Raad voor het kwekersrecht, the Commissie voor de samenstelling van rassenlijst voor landbouwgewassen, the Commissie voor de samenstelling van rassenlijst voor bosbouwgewassen and the Commissie Toelating groenterassen were merged into the Raad voor plantenrassen. Since 1 January 2008 the Raad voor plantenrassen has been supported by the Bureau Administratie en Documentatie of Naktuinbouw, Rassen & Proeven department.

Statutory task: The Raad voor plantenrassen is responsible for:* granting plant breeders' rights;* admitting agricultural varieties;* admitting varieties and stands of forestry crops;* admitting vegetable varieties by means of the so-called B-list. The Raad also holds the Nederlands Rassenregister.

The Raad voor Rechtsbijstand (RvR) is, as an independent administrative body, responsible for providing subsidised legal aid in European Nederland and on Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba. In addition, the RvR implements (part of) the Wet schuldsanering natuurlijke personen (Wsnp) and the Wet beëdigde tolken en vertalers (Wbtv).

Statutory task: The Raad voor Rechtsbijstand (RvR) organises and provides legal aid and mediation, and supervises their delivery. The RvR also coordinates, on behalf of the Minister van Justitie en Veiligheid, the implementation of the Wet schuldsanering natuurlijke personen (Wsnp) and also implements the Wet beëdigde tolken en vertalers (Wbtv).

The RDW (formerly the Rijksdienst voor het Wegverkeer) is a public service provider in the mobility chain. As an independent administrative body, the RDW carries out a number of statutory and assigned tasks in the fields of admission of vehicles and their parts, supervision, enforcement, registration, provision of information and issuing documents. The RDW carries out these tasks in close cooperation with various partners in the mobility chain.

Statutory task: The RDW has four main assignments from the Dutch government:* admission: admitting vehicles and vehicle parts to the Dutch and European market;* supervision and inspection: supervising companies recognised by the RDW and inspecting the technical condition of vehicles;* registration and provision of information: collecting, storing, processing and managing data on vehicles, their owners and vehicle documents, and providing information on this data to interested parties;* issuing documents: issuing documents needed for vehicles or owners, such as registration certificates, driving licences and the APK form.

This zbo is part of the cluster Registratiecommissies KNMG, KNMP, KNMT, FGzPt en V&VN. It concerns the registration committee of the professional organisation Koninklijke Nederlandsche Maatschappij tot bevordering der Geneeskunst (KNMG). The Registratiecommissie Geneeskundig Specialisten (RGS), a body within the KNMG, periodically checks whether medical specialists meet the rules of the College Geneeskundige Specialismen. Doctors who meet these rules can register in a specialist register. The RGS was formed on 1 January 2013 from a merger of three registration committees: the Huisarts, Verpleeghuisarts en arts voor verstandelijk gehandicapten Registratie Commissie (HVRC), the Medisch Specialisten Registratie Commissie (MSRC) and the Sociaal-Geneeskundigen Registratie Commissie (SGRC).

Statutory task: If an organisation of practitioners of a profession as referred to in article 3 of the Wet beroepen in de individuele gezondheidszorg (Wet BIG) has a specialist register for registering practitioners who have acquired special expertise in practising a sub-area of their profession, and a title is attached to it, the Minister van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport may determine that this title is designated as a legally recognised specialist title. An application for this is made by the board of the organisation; the board may delegate this power to a body. This power may be delegated to the body (college) as referred to in article 14, second paragraph, sub d of the Wet BIG. The Registratiecommissie Geneeskundig Specialisten (RGS), as a body within the Koninklijke Nederlandsche Maatschappij tot bevordering der Geneeskunst (KNMG), is responsible for various tasks relating to the registers of medical specialists. These tasks are:* registering medical specialists in a specialist register;* periodically renewing the registrations mentioned above;* removing the registrations mentioned above.

This zbo is part of the cluster Registratiecommissies KNMG, KNMP, KNMT, FGzPt en V&VN. It concerns the registration committee of the professional organisation Verpleegkundigen en Verzorgenden Nederland (V&VN). The Registratiecommissie Specialismen Verpleegkunde (RSV), an independent body within V&VN, is responsible for the registration and re-registration of nurse specialists, on the basis of article 14 of the Wet op de beroepen in de individuele gezondheidszorg (Wet BIG). Designating the specialisms within nursing, setting up registers and drawing up the general rules on this is done by the College Specialismen Verpleegkunde (CSV). The RSV operates the registers and translates the rules of the CSV into practical implementation.

Statutory task: If an organisation of practitioners of a profession as referred to in article 3 of the Wet beroepen in de individuele gezondheidszorg (Wet BIG) has a specialist register for registering practitioners who have acquired special expertise in practising a sub-area of their profession, and a title is attached to it, the Minister van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport may determine that this title is designated as a legally recognised specialist title. An application for this is made by the board of the organisation; the board may delegate this power to a body. This power may be delegated to the body (college) as referred to in article 14, second paragraph, sub d of the Wet BIG. The Registratiecommissie Specialismen Verpleegkunde (RSV), as an independent body within Verpleegkundigen & Verzorgenden Nederland (V&VN), is responsible for various tasks relating to the registers of specialist nurses. These tasks are:* setting up and closing the training registers for nurses training to become specialists;* registering nurse specialists in training in the training registers;* recognising training institutions and practice institutions, head trainers and practice trainers;* supervising compliance with college decisions by trainers and training institutions (among other things through visitation);* setting up and closing the registers for nurse specialists;* registering and re-registering nurse specialists in the specialist registers for Algemene Gezondheidszorg (AGZ) and Geestelijke Gezondheidszorg (GGZ).

This zbo is part of the cluster Registratiecommissies KNMG, KNMP, KNMT, FGzPt en V&VN. It concerns the registration committee of the professional organisation Koninklijke Nederlandse Maatschappij tot bevordering der Tandheelkunde (KNMT). The Registratiecommissie Tandheelkundige Specialismen (RTS), an independent body within the KNMT, is charged with implementing and supervising the rules of the College Tandheelkundige Specialismen (CTS). The CTS rules relate among other things to the training programmes, trainers and training institutions for dental specialists, as well as the requirements for (re-)registration.

Statutory task: If an organisation of practitioners of a profession as referred to in article 3 of the Wet beroepen in de individuele gezondheidszorg (Wet BIG) has a specialist register for registering practitioners who have acquired special expertise in practising a sub-area of their profession, and a title is attached to it, the Minister van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport may determine that this title is designated as a legally recognised specialist title. An application for this is made by the board of the organisation; the board may delegate this power to a body. This power may be delegated to the body (college) as referred to in article 14, second paragraph, sub d of the Wet BIG. The Registratiecommissie Tandheelkundige Specialismen (RTS), as an independent body within the Koninklijke Nederlandse Maatschappij tot bevordering der Tandheelkunde (KNMT), is responsible for various tasks relating to the registers of dental specialists. These tasks include:* keeping a specialist register and a training register for the specialism Mondziekten, Kaak- en Aangezichtschirurgie (MKA);* keeping a specialist register and a training register for the specialism Dento-Maxillaire Orthopaedie (DMO);* supervising the rules of the College Tandheelkundige Specialismen (CTS);* implementing the rules of the CTS.

The professional organisations Koninklijke Nederlandsche Maatschappij tot bevordering der Geneeskunst (KNMG), Koninklijke Nederlandse Maatschappij ter bevordering der Pharmacie (KNMP), Koninklijke Nederlandse Maatschappij tot bevordering der Tandheelkunde (KNMT), Federatie van Gezondheidspsychologen en Psychotherapeuten (FGzPt) and Verpleegkundigen & Verzorgenden Nederland (V&VN) as a whole are not independent administrative bodies belonging to this cluster. The registration committees of these professional organisations are.

Statutory task: If an organisation of practitioners of a profession as referred to in article 3 of the Wet beroepen in de individuele gezondheidszorg (Wet BIG) mentioned above has a specialist register for registering practitioners who have acquired special expertise in practising a sub-area of their profession, and a title is attached to it, the Minister van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport may determine that this title is designated as a legally recognised specialist title. An application for this is made by the board of the organisation; the board may delegate this power to a body. This power may be delegated to the body (college) as referred to in article 14, second paragraph, sub d of the Wet BIG. In short: * registering specialists;* removing the registration of specialists;* suspending the registration of specialists.

Statutory task: The Rijkshavenmeester/the Havenbedrijf Rotterdam carries out nautical management/tasks for the Gemeente Rotterdam and the central government, such as with regard to admission policy, imposing compulsory pilotage on an ad hoc basis, giving orders for fairway marking and giving traffic instructions.

Salland Zorgkantoor B.V. is an implementing body of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), as referred to in article 4.1.1 of that act. This Wlz implementing body also has a care office function.

Statutory task: Salland Zorgkantoor B.V. is responsible for carrying out the tasks described in section 2 of chapter 4 (articles 4.2.1 to 4.2.6) of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz). As a care office, Salland Zorgkantoor B.V. also has a duty of care towards all insured persons living in the region for which Salland Zorgkantoor B.V. has been designated as care office. This duty of care includes providing a personal budget (pgb) and handling the administration or checking of the care provided to insured persons in the region concerned. The extent of that administration or checking is determined by an Algemene Maatregel van Bestuur.

Statutory task: * a. developing and maintaining a national qualification structure aimed at matching the supply of vocational education to the needs of society, partly in light of the labour market for graduates and partly with regard to relevant international developments, among other things by making proposals to the minister of OCW for the qualification files referred to in article 7.2.4, second paragraph,; * b. contributing to an efficient and targeted use of public funds by developing proposals on which vocational programmes qualify for funding from the national treasury; * c. promoting the quality of work-based learning; * d. developing and setting quality criteria for work-based learning places and assessing, at least once every four years, companies and organisations that provide work-based learning against these criteria, and publishing a list of companies and organisations that meet these criteria; * e. ensuring as far as possible the availability of a sufficient number of companies and organisations of adequate quality that provide work-based learning; * f. carrying out research in support of the tasks mentioned above, and; * g. carrying out additional activities to improve the match between education and the labour market;

Skal Biocontrole is the Dutch supervisor of the organic chain. The foundation certifies companies that carry out organic activities and checks whether the production, processing and trade of organic products complies with both Dutch and European rules.

Statutory task: Stichting Skal Biocontrole is designated as the competent authority for carrying out statutory tasks in the field of supervision, inspection and certification arising from the European regulations for a statutory organic quality mark.

The department Sociaal-economische en ruimtelijke statistieken (SER) of the CBS consists of the divisions below, each of which is divided into a number of teams:SBM (Policy and management support):* SIM (Information management)* SBS (Policy staff)SQS (Quaternary sector):* SGZ (Health and care)* SND (Education)* SRV (Legal protection and security)* SCT (Culture, tourism and technology)SLO (Living environment):* SRR (Region and space)* SVW (Real estate and housing market)* SLN (Agriculture and nature)* SMI (Environment)* SEN (Energy)SES (Demographic and socio-economic statistics):* SAM (Labour market)* SDE (Demography)* SOZ (Social security)* SET (Socio-economic overall picture)* CN (Caribisch Nederland)SAL (Labour, income and living conditions):* SPR (Production)* SDV (Dynamic processing)* SAD (Labour, dynamics and mobility)* SIL (Living conditions, income and cohesion)SVV (Traffic and transport):* SGV (Freight transport)* SGP (Passenger transport)The divisions and teams are taken from the [CBS-organogram](https://www.cbs.nl/-/media/_pdf/organogram-nl.pdf).

The Sociale Verzekeringsbank (SVB) has been implementing various schemes in social security and care for some 120 years. These are schemes for different groups of people such as older people, parents, surviving dependants, holders of a personal budget, resistance participants and war victims, and many others. We do this on behalf of governments and other bodies. Our main client is the Ministerie van Sociale Zaken en Werkgelegenheid. We also work for other clients, such as the ministerie van Volksgezondheid Welzijn en Sport.

Statutory task: The Sociale Verzekeringsbank (SVB) has the following tasks:* implementing the Algemene Ouderdomswet, the Algemene nabestaandenwet, the Algemene Kinderbijslagwet and laws governing the implementation of these laws;* ensuring that sound information is provided, on request or unsolicited, to employers, employees, benefit recipients, insured persons and other interested parties in connection with the implementation of the laws mentioned above;* carrying out tasks assigned to the SVB by laws other than those mentioned above;* managing and administering the funds referred to in article 1 Wet structuur uitvoeringsorganisatie werk en inkomen, parts f and g of the Wet financiering sociale verzekeringen and the Algemeen Kinderbijslagfonds, referred to in article 29a of the Algemene Kinderbijslagwet;* carrying out research into the statutory tasks of the SVB on behalf of the minister of Sociale Zaken en Werkgelegenheid (SZW) or on its own initiative;* providing the minister of SZW, at the minister's request, with the information needed to assess the feasibility of policy intentions and statutory rules;* keeping adequate records in order to carry out the tasks of the SVB;* providing services for data exchange with other countries and processing data from other countries;* at the request of an insured person, a health insurer or another interested party, providing information on the insurance status of the insured person (insofar as this information is necessary for implementing the Algemene Wet Bijzondere Ziektekosten and the Zorgverzekeringswet) and, at the request of an insured person, providing information on the insurance periods and the entitlement to old age pension based on them.

This zbo is part of the cluster Registratiecommissies KNMG, KNMP, KNMT, FGzPt en V&VN. The Specialisten Registratie Commissie (SRC) is the registration committee of the professional organisation Koninklijke Nederlandse Maatschappij ter bevordering der Pharmacie (KNMP). The registration committee is a part-time zbo set up under private law with public law tasks. The SRC was set up by the KNMP as supervisor of the quality of the training and the profession of pharmacist. The SRC consists of two chambers: one for community pharmacy (SRC-OF) and one for hospital pharmacy (SRC-ZF).

Statutory task: If an organisation of practitioners of a profession as referred to in article 3 of the Wet beroepen in de individuele gezondheidszorg (Wet BIG) has a specialist register for registering practitioners who have acquired special expertise in practising a sub-area of their profession, and a title is attached to it, the Minister van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport may determine that this title is designated as a legally recognised specialist title. An application for this is made by the board of the organisation; the board may delegate this power to a body. This power may be delegated to the body (college) as referred to in article 14, second paragraph, sub d of the Wet BIG. The Specialisten Registratie Commissie (SRC) was established by the Koninklijke Nederlandse Maatschappij ter bevordering der Pharmacie (KNMP) as supervisor of the quality of the training and the profession of the specialisms of community pharmacist and hospital pharmacist. The tasks of the SRC are:* opening or closing a register as referred to in article 11 under c or e of the Regeling Specialismen en profielen Farmacie 2023, after the Centraal College has decided to establish or withdraw it;* registering a pharmacist in a specialist register and removing the registration;* re-registering a pharmacist in a specialist register, whether or not directly following on, whether or not on the basis of equivalent activities, and removing the registration;* registering the pharmacist in a training register and amending or removing the registration;* issuing a training title if a pharmacist has successfully completed the specialist training in Nederland;* recognising professional qualifications;* recognising or renewing recognition of a trainer or training institution, and amending, suspending or withdrawing the recognition;* supervising compliance with a decision of the Centraal College by a trainer, training institution, training institute or pharmacist in training;* drawing up implementing regulations on the basis of decisions of the Centraal College, concerning training and/or re-registration and/or renewed registration in the specialist register; * supervising the specialist register.

Staatsbosbeheer, founded in 1899, is a legal entity with a statutory task (RWT): managing the land entrusted to it and making it sustainably useful to society.

Statutory task: Managing state forests and nature areas.

The Stichting Administratie Indonesische Pensioenen (SAIP) is an independent administrative body (zbo) under the ministerie van Binnenlandse Zaken (BZK). Its board is formed by a Raad van Beheer, which is charged with managing the foundation's funds and with granting, calculating, paying and administering the overseas pensions and benefits. Under the SAIP's articles of association, the Raad van Beheer accounts to the ministers of BZK and Financiën by means of the annual report. The SAIP has no staff of its own. Under an agreement concluded by the Raad van Beheer with the Stichting Pensioenfonds ABP, the implementation work lies with that pension fund. ABP has in turn assigned the implementation of this work to APG.

Statutory task: The Stichting Administratie Indonesische Pensioenen (SAIP) has the following tasks:* ensuring the fulfilment of the obligation to pay widows' pensions and orphans' allowances to the surviving relatives of former government staff of Indonesië;* taking decisions on behalf of the minister concerned to implement the schemes and matters relating to so-called overseas pensions and benefits.

The Autoriteit Financiële Markten (AFM) ensures that the financial markets operate transparently. The AFM's supervision focuses among other things on saving, investing, insurance, lending, pensions, capital markets, asset management, audit firms and financial reporting. The AFM also supervises financial undertakings in Caribisch Nederland, together with De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).

Statutory task: The main task of the AFM is conduct supervision of the financial markets, to promote an orderly and transparent market process, fair relations between market parties and the protection of consumers. The AFM has this supervisory task under the Wet op het financieel toezicht (Wft). The AFM also decides on the admission of financial undertakings to the financial markets. The AFM supervises financial undertakings in Caribisch Nederland together with De Nederlandse Bank (DNB).

The Stichting Blik op Werk was founded as an independent quality institute and has been designated by the Regeling inburgering 2021 as the organisation that awards and manages the Keurmerk Inburgeren.

Statutory task: Blik op Werk grants a quality mark to organisations whose services promote sustainable labour participation and civic integration. The quality of the services provided by quality mark holders is independently checked. Blik op Werk also supports quality mark holders in making their services transparent, visible and findable in the Blik op Werk Kwaliteitsregister.

Since 1923, inspecting flower bulbs has been the core task of the foundation Bloembollenkeuringsdienst (BKD). We inspect for both quality and quarantine infestations. We carry out quality inspections, laboratory testing and import inspections. We also carry out export inspections on behalf of the Nederlandse Voedsel en Waren Autoriteit (NVWA). BKD supports market access by inspecting flower bulbs at a leading level of quality and provides (inter)national guarantees for the quality of flower bulbs. We carry out these inspections in an independent, reliable and efficient way and are therefore an important link in quality assurance for businesses and the flower bulb sector. The BKD is an independent administrative body and we carry out our statutory tasks on behalf of and under the supervision of the ministerie van Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur (LVVN).

Statutory task: The Bloembollenkeuringsdienst carries out phytosanitary and quality inspections of flower bulbs.

The Stichting Controle Orgaan Kwaliteits Zaken (COKZ) is the Dutch supervisor in the field of dairy, poultry and eggs. In carrying out this supervision, the COKZ implements Dutch and European rules. The COKZ is the successor of the Centraal Orgaan Zuivelcontrole (COZ) and the Centraal Orgaan Melkhygiëne (COM). The tasks of the Controlebureau voor Pluimvee, Eieren en Eiproducten (CPE) were also transferred to the COKZ as of 1 July 2012.

Statutory task: The Controle Orgaan Kwaliteits Zaken (COKZ) has, among others, the following tasks:* supervising compliance with process and product quality criteria in the dairy and egg sector;* safeguarding the safety and quality of milk, dairy products, eggs and egg products produced in Nederland;* keeping a register of approved companies (supervised by the COKZ) and making it available to the Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit (NVWA).

Our mission: Culture does something. It has a connecting, inspiring and stimulating power. The Fonds voor Cultuurparticipatie supports the cultural sector in achieving active participation in art and culture by as many Dutch people as possible, including those for whom taking part in culture is not a matter of course. The Fonds contributes to a resilient, agile and future-proof sector that can make full use of the thinking and making power of culture for our society. Active participation in culture brings people together, challenges them and offers new perspectives. Art and culture can increase opportunities and reduce differences, broaden views and enrich people. Culture helps you believe in yourself and put yourself in someone else's shoes, creates possibilities and lets you meet like-minded people and people who think differently. From Amsterdam to Appingedam and from Wilnis to Willemstad: culture belongs to every Dutch person. We believe in the positive impact of culture on every individual, with a strong, social and resilient society as a result. An assignment with impact: As a national culture fund, we stimulate active participation in culture in the Koninkrijk der Nederlanden. We do this by contributing to cultural education in and outside school, active cultural participation, accessibility of talent development, active heritage participation and international cooperation. How? To give as many people as possible access to art and culture, we work according to the following principles: Culture close by for everyone: We are committed to a solid cultural infrastructure everywhere in our Koninkrijk, so that culture is accessible to everyone and can be of value to society. We take into account the differences between regions and work with regional and local partners on (local) strengthening. Through them, as a national fund, we are close to our applicants and target groups, we contribute to future-proof ecosystems for art and culture and we can better drive cross-sector cooperation. Offering equal opportunities: In addition, it is of the utmost importance that our cultural policy is fair. This means that we make an extra effort to reach target groups for whom the distance to cultural participation is greater than for others, and that we focus on removing the factors that cause this inequality.

Statutory task: Providing and monitoring subsidies in the field of cultural participation.

Stichting Groene Erkenningen was formed on 1 January 2023 from a merger of the Bureau Erkenningen with Groenkeur. The zbo activities of the foundation continue to operate under the name Bureau Erkenningen. In 2023 the Stichting voor de Plaagdierbeheersing, the Stichting Examen- en Certificeringsinstituut Plaagdierpreventie and the Stichting Certificeringsinstituut Plaagdierbeheersing, Milieu en Volksgezondheid were dissolved. Their activities have been continued by Stichting Groene Erkenningen under the name Register Plaagdierbeheersing, Milieu en Veiligheid (RPMV). This activity is also a statutory task that the foundation carries out. The foundation has been appointed by the designated inspection bodies under the WAS2023, transitioning into the WAAS, to draw up and manage a scheme in close consultation with the ministerie van VWS. The private and public tasks are separate activities within the foundation. The foundation is an authority in independently making and managing standards that are self-evident and that demonstrate that work in the living environment is done competently, safely and responsibly.

Statutory task: Stichting Groene Erkenningen is responsible for issuing and recognising, on application, certificates of professional competence in the field of plant protection products and/or biocides.

Statutory task: * The main task of the KCB is inspecting fresh fruit and vegetables, cut flowers and potted plants. The KCB carries out: * import and export inspection (quality) of fresh fruit and vegetables; * quality control of fresh fruit and vegetables traded within Nederland, with the exception of the retail stage; * import inspection (phytosanitary) of fresh fruit and vegetables, cut flowers and potted plants and of plant products that do not fall under a specific sector, also called 'miscellaneous products'; * sampling and monitoring activities for export to specific destinations, including the 'Monitoring vruchtgroenten' intended for Japan, USA and Canada.; * In addition, the KCB carries out a number of projects for the government, such as Survey Tuta Absoluta in the final cultivation of tomato and Survey Afrikaanse fruitmot in the final cultivation of sweet pepper. The phytosanitary export inspection of plant products and the issuing of phytosanitary export certificates are carried out by NVWA officials.; * The endorsement of phytosanitary certificates with a CITES annotation is also carried out by NVWA officials. The KCB receives applications for phytosanitary export inspections and requests for the issue of phytosanitary export certificates.;
Statutory task: Milieukeur is responsible for issuing an EU ecolabel.

Statutory task: Stimulating film production in the Netherlands, with an emphasis on quality and diversity, and promoting a good climate for Dutch film culture. To achieve this, the Fonds gives filmmakers financial support in developing, making and distributing films. The Fonds is involved in the making of feature films, documentary films, experimental films, short films and animated films. In addition, the Fonds has money for special activities in the field of film.
Statutory task: Granting subsidies to artists and institutions for activities aimed at creating, producing, presenting and consuming performing arts.

The Nederlands Jeugdinstituut (NJi) is a national knowledge centre that works to give every child a promising youth. To reach that goal, the NJi collects knowledge about growing up and enriches, interprets and shares it. The NJi also helps apply the collected knowledge and manages the implementation of the part of the Erasmus programme that relates to youth, as laid down in the Uitvoeringsbesluit Uitvoeringswet Erasmusprogramma en programma Europees Solidariteitskorps VWS.

Statutory task: The Nederlands Jeugdinstituut (NJi) has the following tasks:* collecting current knowledge about how children grow up;* enriching, interpreting and sharing this knowledge;* drawing attention to the collected knowledge and helping to apply it;* managing the implementation of the Erasmus programme, where this relates to youth.

The Nederlands Letterenfonds was formed in 2010 from a merger of the Stichting Fonds voor de Letteren and the Stichting Nederlands Literair Productie- en Vertalingenfonds.

Statutory task: The main objective of the Nederlands Letterenfonds is to promote the following:* the quality and diversity of Dutch, Frisian and Papiamento language literature and the quality and diversity of literary works in Dutch Sign Language;* the quality and diversity of literature from other language areas in Dutch, Frisian or Papiamento translation or in translation into Dutch Sign Language;* the translation of high quality original Dutch, Frisian and Papiamento language literary works and literary works in Dutch Sign Language into languages other than Dutch, Frisian and Papiamento, as well as the international distribution of these translations and furthermore everything related to this or that may contribute to it.

The Nederlandse Algemene Keuringsdienst voor zaaizaad en pootgoed van landbouwgewassen carries out statutory inspections on behalf of and under the supervision of the ministerie van Landbouw, Natuur en Voedselkwaliteit. Among other things, potatoes, soil and seeds are assessed on various quality characteristics.

Statutory task: * Promoting, by means of inspections, that reliable propagating material of agricultural crops is placed on the market, traded further and exported;* issuing certificates as proof of approval;* supervising compliance with the regulations;* carrying out phytosanitary export and import inspections and authenticating the phytosanitary certificate.

The Stichting Nederlandse Algemene Kwaliteitsdienst Tuinbouw (Naktuinbouw) was formed on 1 January 2000 from a merger of the Stichting Nederlandse Algemene Keuringsdienst voor Bloemisterij en Boomkwekerijgewassen with the Stichting Nederlandse Algemene Keuringsdienst voor Groente- en Bloemzaden. Naktuinbouw examines propagating material (such as seeds, cuttings and young plants) and new plant varieties produced by horticultural businesses. In addition, Naktuinbouw inspects seed and plant material and tests it for diseases and pests.

Statutory task: * Promotes and safeguards the quality of products, processes and chains in horticulture focused on propagating material, both nationally and internationally. * Carrying out phytosanitary export and import inspections and authenticating the phytosanitary certificate.

Statutory task: Carrying out guardianship for unaccompanied minor asylum seekers and family guardianship for minor children who stay in a reception centre of the Centraal Orgaan opvang asielzoekers (COA).

Vervangingsfonds and Participatiefonds (VfPf) are two independent administrative bodies that are closely intertwined. We work from statutory tasks set out in the Wet op het primair onderwijs. VfPf is the HRM expert that advises and supports schools in their ambitions and development into future-proof and professional organisations.The best education for children comes about in well-functioning school organisations where everyone enjoys working and keeps doing so. VfPf advises and supports school boards in strengthening their responsibility to keep employees sustainably employable within the sector. So that absenteeism and unemployment are as low as possible. We do this with our expertise and experience from inside and outside the education field. We believe in sustainable solutions and always offer customised support, tailored to regional needs. Where necessary, VfPf absorbs the financial consequences of absenteeism and unemployment and quickly guides benefit recipients to a suitable new job. VfPf is of and for primary education and works on a not-for-profit basis. Together with school boards, we work on an attractive and vital sector.

Statutory task: Ensuring reimbursement of the costs related to unemployment benefits for education staff in primary and secondary education.

The Regionale Publieke Omroep (RPO) is a foundation established by the Mediawet that promotes cooperation between public broadcasters in different regions. In addition, the RPO acts as a coordinating body for these broadcasters.

Statutory task: The main tasks of the Regionale Publieke Omroep (RPO) are:* promoting cooperation between public broadcasters at regional level;* coordinating public broadcasters at regional level, with a view to carrying out their public media remit* looking after matters of common interest to the regional public media service and the regional public media institutions;* concluding collective labour agreements and setting payment standards for work supplied by freelancers, partly on behalf of the regional public media institutions;* promoting efficient use of money intended for producing and distributing media content, as well as promoting integrated financial reporting and accountability;* setting up, maintaining, managing, operating and regulating the use of bodies, services and facilities (such as studios and distribution infrastructures) needed for proper performance of the public media remit at regional level.

The Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie is the national cultural fund for design, architecture and digital culture. The task of the Stimuleringsfonds is, from a cultural perspective, to continue and renew the rich design tradition of the Netherlands by stimulating the process of experimenting, researching and making, and by promoting good commissioning.

Statutory task: The fund supports designers and makers with (inter)national projects, cultural institutions with one-year and multi-year programmes, and talents in the creative industry. Its core task is stimulating culture. An important theme is improving the chain between designers/makers and clients/producers. With programmes, events, publications and knowledge pooling, the fund also actively makes connections itself between culture, entrepreneurship and social engagement.

Vervangingsfonds and Participatiefonds (VfPf) are two independent administrative bodies that are closely intertwined. We work from statutory tasks set out in the Wet op het primair onderwijs. VfPf is the HRM expert that advises and supports schools in their ambitions and development into future-proof and professional organisations.The best education for children comes about in well-functioning school organisations where everyone enjoys working and keeps doing so.VfPf advises and supports school boards in strengthening their responsibility to keep employees sustainably employable within the sector. So that absenteeism and unemployment are as low as possible. We do this with our expertise and experience from inside and outside the education field.We believe in sustainable solutions and always offer customised support, tailored to regional needs.Where necessary, VfPf absorbs the financial consequences of absenteeism and unemployment and quickly guides benefit recipients to a suitable new job.VfPf is of and for primary education and works on a not-for-profit basis. Together with school boards, we work on an attractive and vital sector.

Statutory task: Ensuring reimbursement of the costs related to replacing staff of educational institutions in primary and secondary education.

In 2015 (on the basis of Woningwet art. 53a) the minister designated SVWN as the independent body that accredits visitation agencies. In addition, we develop and manage the visitation methodology and supervise the quality of visitations. SVWN also publishes all visitation reports.

Statutory task: * The independent body has the task of ensuring that a visitation can be carried out at housing corporations once every four years, specifically by designating 'expert bodies'. SVWN does this by accrediting agencies that may carry out visitations. (see also art. 2 of the Statuten).

Stichting Wlz-uitvoerder Zorg en Zekerheid is an implementing body of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), as referred to in article 4.1.1 of that law. This Wlz implementing body also has a care office (zorgkantoor) function.

Statutory task: Stichting Wlz-uitvoerder Zorg en Zekerheid is responsible for carrying out the tasks described in section 2 of chapter 4 (articles 4.2.1 to 4.2.6 inclusive) of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz). As a care office, Stichting Wlz-uitvoerder Zorg en Zekerheid also has a duty of care towards all insured persons living in the region for which Stichting Wlz-uitvoerder Zorg en Zekerheid has been designated as care office. This duty of care includes, among other things, providing a personal budget (pgb) and handling the administration or checking of the care provided to insured persons in the region concerned. The extent of that administration or checking is determined by an Algemene Maatregel van Bestuur.

Stichting Zorgkantoor Menzis is an implementing body of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), as referred to in article 4.1.1 of that law. This Wlz implementing body also has a care office (zorgkantoor) function.

Statutory task: Stichting Zorgkantoor Menzis is responsible for carrying out the tasks described in section 2 of chapter 4 (articles 4.2.1 to 4.2.6 inclusive) of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz). As a care office, Stichting Zorgkantoor Menzis also has a duty of care towards all insured persons living in the region for which Stichting Zorgkantoor Menzis has been designated as care office. This duty of care includes, among other things, providing a personal budget (pgb) and handling the administration or checking of the care provided to insured persons in the region concerned. The extent of that administration or checking is determined by an Algemene Maatregel van Bestuur.

The Stimuleringsfonds voor de Journalistiek stimulates the quality, diversity and independence of journalism by promoting the renewal of the journalistic infrastructure in the Netherlands with money, knowledge and research. It does this, among other things, through subsidy schemes, research and by organising events on innovation, investigative journalism and regional and local journalism. In addition, the Fonds shares the latest developments in the journalism sector via the news page on its website.As an independent administrative body (ZBO), the Stimuleringsfonds receives an annual contribution from the ministerie van Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap, from which all activities are funded.

Statutory task: The Stimuleringsfonds voor de Journalistiek (SvdJ) has the following tasks:* maintaining and promoting the pluriformity of the press, insofar as it matters for informing the public and forming opinion;* providing financial support to the press;* carrying out or commissioning research into the functioning of the press.

The Netherlands must be able to trust the quality of construction. That is what the Toelatingsorganisatie Kwaliteitsborging Bouw (TloKB) works on every day. The TloKB supervises quality assurance in construction, recognises the quality of construction products and registers certificates for work on gas combustion installations.As a public, independent party, the TloKB supervises the building quality system as a whole and enforces where necessary. It always does so carefully and transparently. With an eye for the public interest of building quality. Because that is what the TloKB stands for: better trust in the quality of construction.

Statutory task: The Toelatingsorganisatie Kwaliteitsborging Bouw (TloKB) carries out various subtasks in three main areas. These main areas are as follows:* quality assurance;* recognised quality declarations;* work on gas combustion installations.

This is a cluster of independent administrative bodies to which the Kaderwet zelfstandige bestuursorganen does not apply. It concerns health insurers admitted by the Nederlandse Zorgautoriteit as implementing bodies of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), some of which also act as a care office (zorgkantoor).

Statutory task: Efficient and qualitatively sound implementation of the Wet langdurige zorg, in particular carrying out the duty of care for their own insured persons.

UWV is a vital part of society and works for everyone on the labour market. We work to prevent unemployment and incapacity for work. We do this by applying the human touch more often in our services. By further improving our services. By working together with our external partners.

VGZ Zorgkantoor B.V. is an implementing body of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), as referred to in article 4.1.1 of that law. This Wlz implementing body also has a care office (zorgkantoor) function.

Statutory task: VGZ Zorgkantoor B.V. is responsible for carrying out the tasks described in section 2 of chapter 4 (articles 4.2.1 to 4.2.6 inclusive) of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz). As a care office, VGZ Zorgkantoor B.V. also has a duty of care towards all insured persons living in the region for which VGZ Zorgkantoor B.V. has been designated as care office. This duty of care includes, among other things, providing a personal budget (pgb) and handling the administration or checking of the care provided to insured persons in the region concerned. The extent of that administration or checking is determined by an Algemene Maatregel van Bestuur.

This is a cluster consisting of independent administrative bodies that do not fall under the Kaderwet zelfstandige bestuursorganen. The underlying parts of this cluster are therefore not named in the Register van Overheidsorganisaties.

This organisation is part of the Waarborginstellingen cluster.

Statutory task: Assaying submitted objects for their platinum, gold, palladium and silver content and hallmarking these articles.

This cluster comprises the assay offices Edelmetaal Waarborg Nederland B.V. (EWN) and WaarborgHolland B.V., which are responsible for assaying submitted articles for their platinum, gold, palladium and silver content, as well as hallmarking these articles.

Statutory task: Assaying submitted objects for their platinum, gold, palladium and silver content and hallmarking these articles.

The Waarderingskamer checks whether Dutch municipalities implement the Wet waardering onroerende zaken (Wet WOZ) correctly.

Statutory task: The main tasks of the Waarderingskamer are:* supervising the valuation and the determination of the value of real estate (with a view to taxation by the Rijk, the municipalities and the water boards) and the other subjects regulated in the Wet WOZ, so that various taxes can be levied equitably and efficiently;* advising the staatssecretaris van Financiën, on request or on its own initiative, on legislation, regulations and policy regarding the Wet WOZ, as well as developments in the field of the WOZ;* handling disputes between municipalities and other users of value data (such as the Rijk and the water boards) about the implementation of the Wet WOZ;* providing information to municipalities and other WOZ stakeholders.

Zilveren Kruis Zorgkantoor N.V. is an implementing body of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), as referred to in article 4.1.1 of that law. This Wlz implementing body also has a care office (zorgkantoor) function.

Statutory task: Zilveren Kruis Zorgkantoor N.V. is responsible for carrying out the tasks described in section 2 of chapter 4 (articles 4.2.1 to 4.2.6 inclusive) of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz). With all kinds of subsidy programmes we stimulate and fund knowledge development in the field of health, care and wellbeing. In addition, we stimulate the use of the knowledge developed and identify where knowledge is needed. In this way we keep responding to the changing world around us.We increase the relevance, quality and impact of knowledge and innovations and speed up practical applications in order to contribute to good health for everyone. As an organisation we support the entire knowledge chain: from fundamental research, to practice-oriented and action research, to implementation projects.Socially relevant themes are central within the organisation. These themes are carried out, in the form of programmes, within various clusters. Each cluster has its own team with a manager. The staff departments Beleid, Advies en Strategie (BAS) and Bedrijfsvoering support the organisation. The organisation as a whole is led by general director Véronique Timmerhuis. She works together with the management team, which consists of two programme directors, who direct the content clusters, and the heads of department of BAS and Bedrijfsvoering. The ZonMw board is the highest governing body of ZonMw.

Statutory task: ZonMw is an intermediary organisation that has projects, experiments, research and development in the field of health, prevention and care carried out in a programmatic way. ZonMW safeguards their quality, relevance and coherence. The activities cover the entire continuum from fundamental medical research up to and including application and implementation of research projects. The main commissioning parties are the ministerie van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport (VWS) and the Nederlandse Organisatie voor Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek (NWO).

The labour market covers employment, working conditions, participation, benefits and pensions. Responsibility lies with the Minister of Social Affairs and Employment and the Minister for Work and Participation, with UWV, SVB and the Nederlandse Arbeidsinspectie carrying out the work.

Asylum and migration covers asylum procedures, the reception of asylum seekers, family reunification and return. Responsibility lies with the Minister for Asylum and Migration and the State Secretary for Justice and Security, with the IND, the COA and the DT&V carrying out the work.

Infrastructure covers roads, rail, water, shipping, aviation and public transport. Responsibility lies with the Minister and the State Secretary for Infrastructure and Water Management, with Rijkswaterstaat and the KNMI carrying out the work.

Climate and energy covers climate policy, the energy transition, the congested power grid, nuclear energy and making industry sustainable. Responsibility lies with the Minister and the State Secretary for Climate and Green Growth and the Minister of Economic Affairs and Climate.

Kingdom relations covers the relations between the Netherlands and Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten, and the administration of the Caribbean Netherlands. Responsibility lies with the State Secretary for Kingdom Relations and Effective Government at the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations.

Education covers primary and secondary education, vocational education, higher education and science. Responsibility lies with the Minister of Education, Culture and Science and the State Secretary for Education and Emancipation, with DUO and the Onderwijsinspectie carrying out the work.

Public administration and democracy covers how public administration is organised, elections, the relation between central government and the other tiers of government, and the democratic rule of law. Responsibility lies with the Minister of the Interior and Kingdom Relations and the State Secretary for Kingdom Relations and Effective Government, with the Kiesraad and parliament as core institutions.

Nitrogen and agriculture covers the nitrogen approach, nature restoration, the agricultural transition, fisheries and food security. Responsibility lies with the Minister and the State Secretary for Agriculture, Fisheries, Food Security and Nature, with the NVWA and Staatsbosbeheer carrying out the work.

Benefits covers the administration of allowances and the recovery after the childcare benefits scandal, with tailored support and aftercare for affected parents. Responsibility lies with the Minister of Finance and the State Secretary for Benefits Recovery, with Dienst Toeslagen and the Belastingdienst carrying out the work.

Security covers the police, justice, fighting crime, counter-terrorism and law enforcement. Responsibility lies with the Minister and the State Secretary for Justice and Security, with the Politie, the Openbaar Ministerie and the judiciary.

Housing covers sufficient and affordable housing, house building and the allocation of the available space. The policy falls under the Minister of Housing and Spatial Planning at the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations.

Health care covers curative and long-term care, youth care, public health and the accessibility of the health care system. Responsibility lies with the Minister of Health, Welfare and Sport and the Minister for Long-term Care, Youth and Sport.
